title: Pawn steps
objective: Move a white pawn forward, then capture diagonally.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original beginner lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original practice position and teaching text; not a historical game

steps.explanation: A white pawn moves toward the top of this board. Move into an empty square straight ahead.
steps.detail: You can ask for a hint or an answer if you need one.
steps.coach_prompt: Take one step at a time.

question.prompt: Move the white pawn from e2 to e3.
hints: Find the white pawn above your king.

tree.feedback: Yes. Your pawn moved one square straight forward into an empty square.
Two squares is legal from the starting square when both squares are clear. This time, take just one step to e3.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move is legal. Try the destination named in the question.

steps.explanation: The black pawn moved closer. Pawns capture one square diagonally forward, by landing on the other piece.
steps.detail: You can ask for a hint or an answer if you need one.
steps.coach_prompt: Look for a capture on your own.

question.prompt: Capture the black pawn with your pawn.
hints: Look one square diagonally ahead of your pawn.

tree.feedback: Yes. Your pawn captured diagonally. The black pawn is gone and your pawn is on d4.
Moving straight forward is legal here, but it does not capture the black pawn. Look diagonally.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move is legal, but it does not make the capture in this exercise. Look for a capture with your pawn.

takeaway: Pawns move straight forward into empty squares and capture one square diagonally forward.
